findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an explicit pre-apply guard for the value_wo hazard (it is invisible in the plan diff): confirm no value_wo_version bump is in scope and that adopted SecureString params will not be re-sent CHANGEME — do not rely on the 6/1/0 diff-count check alone, since it cannot detect a write-only re-send.
evidence: Plan: 'The apply must stop without mutation if a fresh plan shows destroys or changes outside the approved 6-add/1-change/0-destroy scope.'
ssm.tf:104-105 'value_wo = "CHANGEME" / value_wo_version = 1'; header comment ssm.tf:10-16 'value_wo is, by provider design, NEVER persisted ... re-sends value_wo only when value_wo_version changes'

Parent ticket dd30 comment (ts 1788044999): 'a clean apply here now shares the SAME physical apply as the value_wo migration on origin/main:ssm.tf, which would overwrite all 21 prod SecureString secrets with the CHANGEME placeholder (write-only arg, invisible in the plan diff) -> prod auth/signing/reconcile outage.'
findings.finding: The plan's sole apply-safety mechanism (stop if a fresh plan shows destroys or changes outside 6-add/1-change/0-destroy) keys entirely on the VISIBLE plan diff, but the load-bearing hazard the parent bug deferred this apply for — the value_wo (ADR 0105) write-only re-send that would overwrite live prod SecureString secrets with the CHANGEME placeholder — is by provider design INVISIBLE in the plan diff. The stop-condition cannot detect it, so a plan reading exactly 6/1/0 can still clobber secrets on apply.
findings.location: Verification section + 'Operator Approval and Scope' (stop-condition); ssm.tf:1-18, 95-110 (value_wo)
scenarios: A fresh plan shows 6 add / 1 change / 0 destroy; the operator proceeds; apply re-sends value_wo=CHANGEME to already-seeded SecureString params whose recorded value_wo_version differs, silently overwriting live secrets.
findings.suggested_fix: State that before apply the operator must diff value_wo_version across all rebar_secrets/rebar_plain_seeded resources against recorded state (or coordinate with the 097b value_wo cutover to re-seed real values in-window), and treat any pending value_wo_version change as an out-of-scope STOP even though it does not surface as a diff 'change' line.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider a targeted apply (`-target` on the two mcp alarms, mcp-tickets-pat, and aws_instance.gerrit) to exclude the value_wo-bearing SecureString resources from this window, because the shared ssm.tf apply is the source of the deferred secret-clobber hazard.
evidence: Plan applies the whole recorded plan as one physical apply; parent ticket repeatedly flags that this apply is entangled with the value_wo migration on the same ssm.tf
No consideration of -target or a split apply appears anywhere in the plan
findings.finding: The plan does not weigh a lower-blast-radius alternative to a full `terraform apply`: a targeted apply (`-target`) scoped to just the two CloudWatch alarms, the mcp-tickets-pat create, and the aws_instance.gerrit user_data change. Given the value_wo bulk-re-send hazard on the shared ssm.tf apply, a targeted apply would structurally exclude the risky SecureString resources from this window, which is defensibly superior on blast-radius and robustness.
findings.location: Verification / Operator Approval and Scope (apply mechanism)
scenarios: Operator wants the two alarms + gerrit user_data change but must not touch SecureString value_wo in this window; a full apply forces both together.
